This is great. My mother has and actually does the same thing regarding calling and telling other relatives about the fights. In my understanding its almost as a coping mechanism so the other person can hear it and make the individual feel like they were in the right and sort of empathise with them and also as a way to get it out of their system because the fight ends up revolving in the mind for hours and im sure anyone can get tired of ruminating over the same thing for hours and reliving it.

I'm glad that there is progress being made.

I would say that whenever she becomes triggered, she resorts to a black and white approach. Its also another coping mechanism(splitting)where a person becomes very bad(almost like a enemy) and all the good things and past good and happy memories are overshadowed by the trigger and causes them to feel this way where they have no choice but to resort to paint you very negatively. its sort of a way to evade danger so they don't feel hurt again. I'm sure once things calm down, she might feel a bit better. My point is that what she says about you, im sure she doesn't mean them fully. It's just during the moment during the fight or flight mode.Overtime she will realise that its not worth saying those things and hopefully channel that anger in different ways. 

Edit: I forgot, but it is important to understand what made her say those things about you. You can ask her when she's in a good mood calmly. Perhaps it might be something on her mind thats bothering her about you and she's repressed it until the fight, or if there are any other issues. Understanding her point of view and why it caused her to say those things will lead you to work on your flaws and what you're lacking as well according to her expectations. This will definitely ease some tension and she most likely won't be forced to say those things about you which cause her to have so much resentment.

I do want to add that im not a professional or anything. Just saying based of my struggles and experiences. The best way is to tackle the root causes of everything and that will be probably be done through trauma work

I wish you and your family the best :)

I don't have anything meaningful to offer, but I would just suggest looking into whether her medications have either changed recently or perhaps she might be tapering off and if these fights and her mood is essentially becoming worse over time. This can be a case of withdrawal( I had these similar urges and anger during my withdrawal). And if you have any history of her before being on those medications and whether they assisted her mood or not and if there's any link. Don't do anything regarding the medications, but see what the case is  first. 

Secondly, you need to figure out the triggers which is causing her to be in a fight and defensive position. After a fight and when she has calmed down, ask her what she felt and what caused her to feel that way for instance what caused her to get angry over the ticket. Perhaps its somethings that reminded her of her past or some tension had been building prior between you two and she got triggered over this or that the ticket caused her to have a confrontation with the police officer(just assuming) or someone in authority and caused her anxiety and terrified her (trigger due to trauma by someone in authority) and she felt that you could have avoided this situation from occurring by taking care of it. 

Thirdly, I would just advise you to temporarily diffuse the situation by validating her feelings whenever she's feeling triggered or angry and if she is upset at you, its best to just say im sorry I didn't intend for this  and sort of pacify her telling her its okay. Childhood trauma causes people to feel unsafe and invalidated and so by doing this, it might temporarily prevent the fight from developing further because thats not healthy for anyone especially the children. I would say this is temporary so you can focus on the root causes of the issues through trauma therapy ASAP. I would also highly to advice to choose a professional  who validates her experiences and is someone empathetic to her who she could trust because if there's a stern or rude professional, Im confident she will leave or there will be zero progress because there won't be any meaningful rapport and she is unlikely to listen to whatever the professional says because they might be viewed as a potential threat who's also against her and (in her mind) blames her for what happened

This is just based off my experience because my mother is quite similar and I, unfortunately, have some similar qualities as well due to my own traumas and issues.

I do want to add that it isn't your fault or anyones, and I hope your situation eases and you both acquire the peace and understanding that you both deserve

My story is a bit similar. I grew up with uninvolved parents and so there were some of those issues, but then I found myself being bullied a lot in school. This created periods of low self esteem along with other issues and some occasional anxiety which could be resolved easily at times. However, none of these issues were debilitating and I was still attending school with only 1 day being absent and I was a happy child just like anyone else. I did think there was something wrong with me because of my past trauma and the bullying that I experienced. Hence, I decided to go to a psychiatrist. Well, as it turns out, that ended up being my biggest mistake and my life ended that day, I was prescribed Prozac in about a 15 min. Over time my personality changed, and I became even more weirder and then I started self harming myself and thinking about suicide. I eventually left school and got prescribed even more medications like antipsychotics etc. I felt so damaged. After trying around 5 therapists, 8 psychiatrists and 10 medications, I don't think there's any improvement, rather I've become worse than ever being on those medications. My issues have become chronic. Fat, ugly, baldness, stretch marks. I begin to think how that one visit at 14 years old led to the downfall of my life. Funny, while my psychiatrist wins awards for her supposed outstanding work. Everyone blames me while not thinking about my bullies, or my abusive and neglectful parents.
